# vetkit

> vetkit is a TypeScript library and CLI (`vet`) that generates, validates and runs LLM evals: a generator model drafts criteria and cases, a typed-decision judge scores them, and every verdict records which model answered.

## Install

- Add it to a project with `npm i -D vetkit` (pnpm, yarn and bun equivalents work), then run `npx vetkit init`; it needs Node 22.18 or newer.
- [CLI package README](packages/cli/README.md): commands and first run.
- [Agent setup skill](skills/vetkit-setup/SKILL.md): init, run and a CI step, for an agent to follow.

## Quickstart

- `npx vetkit init` writes a runnable example with an offline demo judge; no key is needed.
- `npx vetkit run --json` judges the cases and prints one JSON document; read its `summary`. Demo verdicts are labelled demo and never gate a build.
- To use a real judge, ask the human to add the key to `.env`, then run `npx vetkit init --force`.
- [JSONL example](examples/jsonl/README.md): criteria, cases and traces you can run as is.

## Configuration

- [Config schema](https://melsovcozy.github.io/vetkit/schemas/config.schema.json): JSON Schema for vetkit.config.ts.
- [Configuration reference](docs/configuration.md): every config key and environment variable.
- [Sinks](docs/sinks.md): send verdicts to Langfuse or OpenTelemetry.

## CLI reference

- `vet doctor`: check environment, judge credentials and judge endpoint health
- `vet label`: import human labels from CSV or collect them in a terminal loop
- `vet run`: judge every case against the criteria and exit with the result
- `vet rerun`: re-judge the disputed verdicts (borderline or judge failure) of the last vet run
- `vet report`: render the last run as Markdown and HTML report files without judging
- `vet validate`: calibrate every criterion against human labels and write criteria.lock.json
- `vet estimate`: estimate judge calls, tokens, cost and minutes, with no network call
- `vet init`: scaffold a runnable example, or generate criteria and cases from --source traces
- `vet check`: check criteria.lock.json and the sink outbox against the current project
- `vet lock`: maintain criteria.lock.json
- `vet cache`: verdict cache maintenance
- `vet criteria`: disable, enable, delete or revalidate one criterion in criteria.yaml and the lock
- `vet cases`: secondary case-set actions: dedupe, quarantine, promote, review
- `vet lint`: lint criteria.yaml against Jev wording weak spots (default: criteria.yaml next to the config, or under evals/ when that directory exists)
- `vet export`: export criteria, cases and the lock to another eval runner
- `vet watch`: sample live OTel traces, judge them, and promote failures into regression cases

Every command prints one JSON document under `--json`; the shapes are in [CLI JSON shapes](docs/guides/cli-json.md).

## Integrations

- [AI SDK telemetry guide](docs/guides/ai-sdk-telemetry.md): send `experimental_telemetry` spans to `vet watch`.
- [OTLP over http/json guide](docs/guides/otlp-http-json.md): the receiver accepts JSON only, protobuf gets a 415.
- [AI SDK OTLP example](examples/ai-sdk-otlp/README.md): runs offline with a mock model.
- [JSONL example](examples/jsonl/README.md): own-format traces and hand-written cases.
- [Scorers README](packages/scorers/README.md): vitest matchers and a promptfoo assertion.
- [Watch](docs/watch.md): sample live traffic and promote failures into cases.
